report:
PASS for the entire continuation218 partial manuscript under the accepted caller grant O. This establishes its stated strict winner locality, ordinary open locality, mixed comparison and separately derived pure comparison. It does not close original P16.4. The domain remains actual fixed-L finite-energy potentials on smooth geometrically integral projective X of dimension n≥1, with an actual ample rational L, over every complete characteristic-zero real-valued non-Archimedean field. No algebraic-closure, discreteness, residue-characteristic-zero, metrizability or support condition enters the new conclusions.

The unindexed task passage records the authorization of O; task grants are excluded from the numbered external premises. I checked each application against O's supplied complete body, including its harmless clarifications. O supplies actual endpoint approximation, admissible convex combinations, canonical positive mixed outputs of mass V=(L^n), symmetry, constant invariance, every-E1-test integrability and joint weighted decreasing-net continuity. Its hypotheses hold for every output and test used here. Locality and comparison are established by the new arguments rather than imported from O.

I independently opened the literal BE2021v3 and CLD2012v1 PDFs, verified their version headers, and checked the pertinent complete proof units: BE's FS maximum construction, decreasing closure, smooth regularization and continuous mixed-measure extension; CLD's compact smooth-test machinery, Green formula, local product construction, measure injectivity, approachable metric definition and curvature gluing. The additional analytification premise was checked in Berkovich's own notes. The ledger and historical review labels were not treated as mathematical evidence.

Finite maxima require a small attribution clarification: their E1 closure is derived in continuation218, rather than being an explicitly stated theorem conclusion of O. BE gives actual psh closure under maxima. Since m=max(u,v)≥u, its continuous-majorant set is contained in that of u, so E(m)≥E(u)>−∞. A constant continuous majorant bounds E(m) above. Real constant shifts preserve the actual cone and satisfy E(u+c)=E(u)+cV by the majorant bijection. These establish every maximum and shift used later. Winner sets are Borel by rational-level descriptions of inequalities between extended-real Borel functions. For each individual output, O annihilates the pole sets of the finitely many relevant tests. All subtractions and nonlinear evaluations occur on that output's finite-value full-measure domain.

For continuous locality, global uniform smooth regularization supplies exactly locally psh-approachable weights. A uniformly convergent net permits selection of a sequence with errors below 2^−j; this requires no cofinal sequence. Restricting absolute metrics to a trivialization preserves the same uniform weight error. For rational L, trivialize an integral multiple dL, divide weights by d, and scale the top product by d^−n. This handles the actual rational bundle without replacing it by a numerical class. No assertion that arbitrary continuous CLD-psh functions are approachable is needed.

I reconstructed the local convergence estimate explicitly. For a compact smooth test α and a compact neighborhood V of its support, choose compactly supported dominating forms A_j such that A_0±α and A_{j+1}±d′d″A_j are weakly positive, using the symmetric part of the test. On finitely many tropical charts, domination follows by bounding evaluations on unit simple vectors against the Euclidean positive form; smooth cutoffs assemble these bounds. Products of positive (1,1)-forms are strongly positive. Successive compact-support integrations by parts therefore give |∫u_0 d′d″u_1⋯d′d″u_p∧α|≤C∏_{j=0}^p||u_j||_V. Telescoping two tuples and transferring each differing Hessian onto α bounds the difference by a constant times the sum of their uniform errors, with the other factors uniformly bounded. This proves convergence, approximation independence, positivity and compatibility on overlaps. In top degree the positive functional gives a Radon measure. Multilinearity and restriction compatibility then give the required local sheaf product.

This reconstruction also addresses source-proof details: the dominating form in CLD Proposition 5.6.2 must retain both positive parts, β_0+β′_0. I did not import its broader strong-decomposition wording for arbitrary test forms; weak domination suffices for the estimate just proved. These are explicit checks of the needed dependency, rather than certification of every unrelated assertion in CLD v1. Its Corollary 5.6.6 is used as a measure statement only in top degree p=n. The subtraction sign in BE Lemma 8.6 is handled exactly as in O's supplied clarification.

An analytic unit has affine logarithmic weight in its tropical coordinate, hence zero Hessian. Consequently curvature and its approximating products agree under changes of trivialization. The global BE measure and local CLD top product have identical values on every compactly supported smooth scalar test: extend the test by zero and use the same global uniform smooth approximation for both limits. Smooth-test injectivity identifies the actual Radon measures. Its proof controls a positive current on a compact set by a smooth cutoff times the uniform norm, extends through compact smooth density, and obtains uniqueness. The carrier and its open subsets are boundaryless, so this identification loses no boundary-supported component. Equality of the maximum's local weight with the winning weight proves both continuous winner identities.

The nonlinear-test lemma is valid for arbitrary directed nets. On a tail, each continuous approximation a_{s,k} has a common upper bound C. The nonnegative continuous functions C−a_{s,k} increase to C−a_s. Their strict open levels form directed covers; Radon inner approximation and finite compact subcovers give the supremum identity for each level. Truncated finite lower layer sums, with one common index for their finitely many levels, establish the integral identity. Endpoint integrability makes subtraction legitimate and gives ∫(a_{s,k}−a_s)dρ→0. For each fixed approximation stage, O's fixed-weight law and weak convergence transport this error integral through ρ_i. Choose one stage for each of the finitely many arguments, then a finite common i-tail. The Lipschitz error is bounded by ||f||∞Lip(F)Σ_s∫(a_{s,k}−a_s)dρ_i, with the analogous bound for ρ. The fixed approximating composition is continuous. For moving arguments, O's moving-weight and fixed-weight laws give ∫(a_{s,i}−a_s)dρ_i→0. This proves both nonlinear convergence statements without measurable-net monotone convergence or intersections of measure-one sets across the net.

For strict locality, the product-directed continuous approximations satisfy m_i=max(u_i,v_i)↓max(u,v). For each fixed ε, the cutoff F_ε(a,b)=χ_ε(a−b) is bounded and Lipschitz and vanishes outside the continuous winner set. Continuous locality therefore gives the cutoff equality for both moving output nets. The nonlinear lemma passes that equality to the endpoints. A bounded nonnegative Borel multiplier preserves finite Radon regularity because its inner and outer approximation errors are bounded by its supremum times the original errors. Equality on continuous tests thus identifies the weighted measures. Only after this identification does ε=1/j decrease: the cutoffs increase to the strict indicator, and convergence is taken separately on each fixed measure. Pole-nullness restores the literal extended-real winner sets.

For open locality, max(u+ε,v) and max(u,v+ε) both decrease to max(u,v). On an open U where u=v pointwise, strict locality identifies their restrictions with MA(u,R) and MA(v,R), respectively, outside null pole sets. Compactly supported continuous tests in U extend by zero to T and pass through O's weak decreasing continuity. Such tests determine Radon restrictions, proving the asserted ordinary open locality. This establishes no locality on an arbitrary Borel coincidence set.

For mixed comparison, fix ε>0, A_ε={u<v−ε}, B_ε={u>v−ε}, and τ_ε=MA(max(u,v−ε),R). Strict locality gives τ_ε|A_ε=MA(v,R)|A_ε and τ_ε|B_ε=MA(u,R)|B_ε. Equal raw masses yield MA(v,R)(A_ε)≤MA(u,R)({u≤v−ε})≤MA(u,R)({u<v}). The last inclusion is applied on the finite-value domain; any common-pole exception has zero measure. Equality-set mass is retained in the upper bound, so no boundary-nullness assumption enters. Letting ε=1/j decrease uses continuity from below solely for the fixed measure MA(v,R). No continuity theorem is applied to the increasing maxima in this comparison argument.

Pure comparison has its required separate proof. For each fixed ε, start with MA(max(u,v−ε),…,max(u,v−ε)). On A_ε, replace its n slots successively by v−ε; on B_ε, replace them successively by u. Symmetry and the proved one-slot strict locality justify each replacement with the remaining actual E1 slots held fixed. Constant invariance produces MA(v) and MA(u). The same raw-mass calculation and fixed-measure limit give pure comparison. Repeating fixed slots in mixed comparison alone would not prove this result. When n=1, the remaining tuple is empty and every argument still applies.

The historical descriptions of O as unreviewed are superseded by the explicit caller grant; this is a harmless status correction. Selecting uniform smooth sequences and interpreting CLD's measure assertion in top degree make implicit qualifications explicit. No substantial repair of continuation218's theorem or proof strategy is required. Original P16.4 still lacks normalized actual-potential compactness, the required arbitrary-field envelope and orthogonality inputs, both-sign outer-direction energy differentiation, an intrinsic prescribed-target finite-energy/finite-dual characterization, actual attainment, and uniqueness of every solution modulo constants. The whole original equation request remains unclosed.

passages.statement: Let K be any complete non-Archimedean real-valued field and L a semiample rational line bundle on a projective K-scheme. The decreasing-FS-net psh class is closed under finite maxima and real constant shifts. Every such psh metric admits a decreasing smooth semipositive approximation net, uniform when its endpoint is continuous. (BE2021v3, §§7.1 and 7.3.)

Let K be any complete non-Archimedean real-valued field and L a semiample rational line bundle on a projective K-scheme. The decreasing-FS-net psh class is closed under finite maxima and real constant shifts. Every such psh metric admits a decreasing smooth semipositive approximation net, uniform when its endpoint is continuous. (BE2021v3, §§7.1 and 7.3.)
passages.quote: Every psh metric φ on a semiample Q-line bundle L is psh-regularizable.

passages.statement: For an n-dimensional projective scheme over any complete non-Archimedean real-valued field and rational line bundles L1,…,Ln, the smooth semipositive mixed curvature measure extends uniquely to continuous psh-regularizable metrics, continuously for uniform metric convergence and weak Radon convergence. The extension is positive, symmetric and multiadditive, with raw intersection mass (L1⋯Ln). (BE2021v3, Theorem 8.4 and Proposition 8.5.)

On a good Hausdorff pure n-dimensional boundaryless analytic space over a complete non-Archimedean field, smooth symmetric forms α of type (p,p) and β of type (q,q), with p+q=n−1 and compact support intersection, satisfy ∫α∧d′d″β=∫d′d″α∧β. (CLD2012v1, Theorem 3.12.2.)
passages.quote: supports de α et β est compact.

passages.statement: Over any complete non-Archimedean field, on a good Hausdorff pure n-dimensional analytic space, n locally psh-approachable functions have a unique positive Radon top product on the interior, continuous under uniform smooth psh approximation against compact smooth tests, symmetric, multilinear and compatible with restrictions; it extends to differences of approachable functions. (CLD2012v1, §5.6.)

Over any complete non-Archimedean field, on a good Hausdorff pure n-dimensional analytic space, n locally psh-approachable functions have a unique positive Radon top product on the interior, continuous under uniform smooth psh approximation against compact smooth tests, symmetric, multilinear and compatible with restrictions; it extends to differences of approachable functions. (CLD2012v1, §5.6.)

On good Hausdorff analytic spaces over a complete non-Archimedean field, compact sets admit smooth cutoffs in prescribed open neighborhoods; compact continuous tests admit uniformly approximating smooth tests there; positive Radon measures on the interior correspond bijectively to positive top currents. (CLD2012v1, §3.3 and Proposition 5.4.6.)

For topologically locally trivial continuous metrized line bundles on good Hausdorff pure-dimensional boundaryless analytic spaces over a complete non-Archimedean field, local weight curvatures glue independently of trivialization, since d′d″log|h|=0 for analytic units h. (CLD2012v1, §6.4.1.)

passages.statement: Over any complete non-Archimedean field, the analytification of a separated finite-type scheme is good, Hausdorff and without boundary; if the scheme is proper, its analytification is compact. (Berkovich, Non-archimedean analytic spaces, Trieste 2009 notes, Definition 3.2.9 and Facts 4.1.1–4.1.4.)
